subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Green, Grey, and Blue Hydrogen
description: A short lesson to help you apply Green, Grey, and Blue Hydrogen.

hook.text: Not all hydrogen is created equal—the color label tells you how clean the production process really is.

buildup.text: Grey hydrogen comes from splitting natural gas, releasing carbon dioxide—this is 95 percent of today's supply.

discovery.text: Blue hydrogen captures that CO2 before it escapes, but capture technology is expensive and imperfect.

twist.text: Green hydrogen uses renewable electricity to split water, producing zero emissions—but it costs three times more.

climax.text: For hydrogen cars to truly be clean, the world needs massive green hydrogen production that doesn't yet exist.

punchline.text: Hydrogen is only as clean as the energy used to make it.

quiz.question: What makes green hydrogen different from grey hydrogen?
options: It's produced using renewable energy with zero emissions
